ESV.1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
ESV.2: “If one ventures a word with you, will you be impatient? Yet who can keep from speaking?
ESV.3: Behold, you have instructed many, and you have strengthened the weak hands.
ESV.4: Your words have upheld him who was stumbling, and you have made firm the feeble knees.
ESV.5: But now it has come to you, and you are impatient; it touches you, and you are dismayed.
ESV.6: Is not your fear of God  your confidence, and the integrity of your ways your hope?
ESV.7: “Remember: who that was innocent ever perished? Or where were the upright cut off?
ESV.8: As I have seen, those who plow iniquity and sow trouble reap the same.
ESV.9: By the breath of God they perish, and by the blast of his anger they are consumed.
ESV.10: The roar of the lion, the voice of the fierce lion, the teeth of the young lions are broken.
ESV.11: The strong lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness are scattered.
ESV.12: “Now a word was brought to me stealthily; my ear received the whisper of it.
ESV.13: Amid thoughts from visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men,
ESV.14: dread came upon me, and trembling, which made all my bones shake.
ESV.15: A spirit glided past my face; the hair of my flesh stood up.
ESV.16: It stood still, but I could not discern its appearance. A form was before my eyes; there was silence, then I heard a voice:
ESV.17: ‘Can mortal man be in the right before  God? Can a man be pure before his Maker?
ESV.18: Even in his servants he puts no trust, and his angels he charges with error;
ESV.19: how much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed like  the moth.
ESV.20: Between morning and evening they are beaten to pieces; they perish forever without anyone regarding it.
ESV.21: Is not their tent-cord plucked up within them, do they not die, and that without wisdom?’

AMP.1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,
AMP.2:
"If we dare to converse with you, will you be impatient [or offended]?
But who can restrain himself from speaking?
AMP.3:
"Behold, you have admonished and instructed many,
And you have strengthened weak hands.
AMP.4:
"Your words have helped the one who was stumbling to stand,
And you have strengthened feeble knees.
AMP.5:
"But now adversity comes upon you, and you are impatient and intolerant;
It touches you, and you are horrified.
AMP.6:
"Is not your fear of God your confidence,
And [is not] the integrity and uprightness of your ways your hope?
AMP.7:
"Remember now, who, being innocent, ever perished?
Or where [and in what circumstances] were those upright and in right standing with God destroyed?
AMP.8:
"As I have seen, those who plow wickedness
And those who sow trouble and harm harvest it.
AMP.9:
"By the breath of God they perish,
And by the blast of His anger they are consumed.
AMP.10:
"The roaring of the lion and the voice of the fierce lion,
And the teeth of the young lions are broken.
AMP.11:
"The lion perishes for lack of prey,
And the cubs of the lioness are scattered.
AMP.12:
"Now a word was secretly brought to me,
And my ear received a whisper of it.
AMP.13:
"Amid disquieting thoughts from the visions of the night,
When deep sleep falls on men,
AMP.14:
Dread and trembling came upon me,
Which made all my bones shake.
AMP.15:
"Then a spirit passed before my face;
The hair on my skin stood on end!
AMP.16:
"The spirit stood still, but I could not discern its appearance;
A form was before my eyes;
There was silence, and then I heard a voice, saying:
AMP.17:
'Can [mortal] man be just before God or be more righteous than He?
Can a man be pure before his Maker or be more cleansed than He?
AMP.18:
'God puts no trust or confidence, even in His [heavenly] servants,
And He charges His angels with error.
AMP.19:
'How much more [will He blame and charge] those who dwell in houses (bodies) of clay,
Whose foundations are in the dust,
Who are crushed like a moth.
AMP.20:
'Between morning and evening they are broken in pieces and destroyed;
Unobserved and unnoticed, they perish forever.
AMP.21:
'Is not their tent-cord drawn up within them [so that the tent collapses]?
Do they not die, and yet without [acquiring] wisdom?'

NLT.1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied to Job:
NLT.2:
“Will you be patient and let me say a word?
For who could keep from speaking out?
NLT.3:
“In the past you have encouraged many people;
you have strengthened those who were weak.
NLT.4:
Your words have supported those who were falling;
you encouraged those with shaky knees.
NLT.5:
But now when trouble strikes, you lose heart.
You are terrified when it touches you.
NLT.6:
Doesn’t your reverence for God give you confidence?
Doesn’t your life of integrity give you hope?
NLT.7:
“Stop and think! Do the innocent die?
When have the upright been destroyed?
NLT.8:
My experience shows that those who plant trouble
and cultivate evil will harvest the same.
NLT.9:
A breath from God destroys them.
They vanish in a blast of his anger.
NLT.10:
The lion roars and the wildcat snarls,
but the teeth of strong lions will be broken.
NLT.11:
The fierce lion will starve for lack of prey,
and the cubs of the lioness will be scattered.
NLT.12:
“This truth was given to me in secret,
as though whispered in my ear.
NLT.13:
It came to me in a disturbing vision at night,
when people are in a deep sleep.
NLT.14:
Fear gripped me,
and my bones trembled.
NLT.15:
A spirit swept past my face,
and my hair stood on end.
NLT.16:
The spirit stopped, but I couldn’t see its shape.
There was a form before my eyes.
In the silence I heard a voice say,
NLT.17:
‘Can a mortal be innocent before God?
Can anyone be pure before the Creator?’
NLT.18:
“If God does not trust his own angels
and has charged his messengers with foolishness,
NLT.19:
how much less will he trust people made of clay!
They are made of dust, crushed as easily as a moth.
NLT.20:
They are alive in the morning but dead by evening,
gone forever without a trace.
NLT.21:
Their tent-cords are pulled and the tent collapses,
and they die in ignorance.

NET.13: In the troubling thoughts of the dreams in the night when a deep sleep falls on men,
NET.14: a trembling gripped me — and a terror! — and made all my bones shake.
NET.15: Then a breath of air passes by my face; it makes the hair of my flesh stand up.
NET.16: It stands still, but I cannot recognize its appearance; an image is before my eyes, and I hear a murmuring voice:
NET.17: “Is a mortal man righteous before God? Or a man pure before his Creator?
NET.18: If God puts no trust in his servants and attributes folly to his angels,
NET.19: how much more to those who live in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed like a moth?
NET.20: They are destroyed between morning and evening; they perish forever without anyone regarding it.
NET.21: Is not their excess wealth taken away from them? They die, yet without attaining wisdom.
